slides.0.title: Diploma Tasting and Essays
slides.0.subtitle: Blind-tasting clues and MW-style essays
slides.1.title: The structure of an SAT tasting note
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Appearance
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Clarity, intensity and colour (including rim). Rhône cues: Grenache paler with early garnet rims; Syrah and Mourvèdre deeper with purple tones
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Nose
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Condition, intensity, aroma characteristics (fruit, floral, spice, oak, age) and development. Organise as primary fruit / oak and winemaking / ageing
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Palate
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Sweetness, acidity, tannin, alcohol, body, flavour intensity, flavour characteristics and finish. For Rhône reds the key is the acidity-tannin-alcohol triangle
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Conclusions
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Quality assessment (justified by balance, length, intensity and complexity) and readiness for drinking or potential for ageing; if asked, then deduce region, variety and style
slides.1.content: Reminder: the SAT lexicon and marking can change, so follow WSET's latest official specification and candidate handbook; the models below only illustrate the writing method.
slides.2.title: Model note A: northern Rhône Syrah (fictional wine)
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Appearance
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Clear; deep intensity; purple-ruby with a purple rim
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Nose
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Clean; pronounced intensity; black pepper, blackberry, blackcurrant, violet, smoke and bacon fat; cedar and vanilla from some oak; youthful
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Palate
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Dry; medium(+) acidity; high, grippy but fine tannin; medium(+) alcohol; full body; pronounced flavour intensity with black fruit, pepper, smoke and oak spice; long finish
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Conclusion
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Quality: very good — balanced, long finish and good complexity; can be drunk now but has clear ageing potential (youthful with firm tannin)
slides.2.highlights.4.title: Deduction
slides.2.highlights.4.content: Pepper + violet + smoke + higher acid and tannin → Syrah in a cool to moderate climate → northern Rhône (for instance Crozes-Hermitage, Cornas or Saint-Joseph style); state why southern Rhône is excluded (acidity, pepper, no sweet ripe red fruit)
slides.2.content: Write deductions as evidence → judgement → reasons for exclusion, not just a region name.
slides.3.title: Model note B: southern Rhône Grenache blend (fictional wine)
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Appearance
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Clear; medium intensity; garnet with a slightly orange rim
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Nose
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Clean; pronounced intensity; ripe red cherry, strawberry jam, garrigue herbs, liquorice and black pepper; some leather and dried fruit; developing
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Palate
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Dry; medium acidity; medium tannin; high alcohol; full body; pronounced flavour intensity of red fruit, spice and herbs; medium(+) finish
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Conclusion
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Quality: good — fruit and spice are well expressed but prominent alcohol slightly reduces balance; ready to drink now and can age a few more years
slides.3.highlights.4.title: Deduction
slides.3.highlights.4.content: Paler colour + orange rim + red fruit + garrigue + high alcohol → Grenache-led, warm Mediterranean climate → southern Rhône (for example Côtes du Rhône Villages, or Gigondas / Châteauneuf-du-Pape style); separate the tier by the balance of acid, tannin and alcohol
slides.3.content: Quick contrast: Syrah's pepper, smoke and acidity versus Grenache's red fruit, herbs and alcohol.
slides.4.title: MW-style essays: three model questions
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Q1: Grenache's role under climate change
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Skeleton: define the problem → strengths (drought tolerance, old vines, southern base) → risks (rising alcohol, falling acidity, pale colour, oxidation) → responses (altitude, picking date, blending, VIFA and non-VIFA varieties) → conclusion: Grenache stays central but shifts from sole lead to being supported by variety mix and viticulture. Evidence: Institut rhodanien phenology and alcohol data (single source, say so)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Q2: Single variety vs blend
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Skeleton: the logic of each model (Cornas 100% Syrah shows the site; Châteauneuf's 13 varieties spread risk and add complexity) → market view (varietal labels are easy to grasp vs communicating appellation names) → climate view (blending adds flexibility) → take a position and acknowledge counter-examples (Côte-Rôtie is Syrah-centred yet permits Viognier)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Q3: Pros and cons of more crus
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Skeleton: factual base (crus promoted since Gigondas in 1971; Laudun became the 18th in 2024) → advantages (value uplift, quality incentive, recognisability) → disadvantages (diluted cru reputation, consumer confusion, boundary with Villages names) → comparison (Burgundy subdivides plots, the Rhône promotes names) → conclusion: clear criteria and ongoing quality review are needed
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Answer technique
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Answer the question first (your position) → evidence (with year and source) → counter-argument → conclusion; one point per paragraph; give years with numbers and do not rest an argument on figures that sources disagree on
slides.4.content: Exam format (question types, numbers, timing and marking) can change, so follow the latest official WSET and IMW specifications; this lesson models thinking structures only.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
What is the standard order of an SAT tasting note?
A. Palate → conclusions → appearance → nose
B. Appearance → nose → palate → conclusions
C. Nose → appearance → conclusions → palate
D. Conclusions → appearance → palate → nose
Appearance → nose → palate → conclusions; deduction of region and variety rests on the conclusions section.
Black pepper, violet, smoke, medium(+) acidity and marked tannin most likely point to?
A. A southern Rhône Grenache blend
B. Northern Rhône Syrah
C. Tavel rosé
D. Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise
This is the classic cue set for northern Rhône Syrah; the answer should also say why southern Rhône is excluded.
Which appellation became the 18th cru in 2024?
A. Cairanne
B. Rasteau
C. Laudun
D. Vinsobres
Laudun, approved by the INAO national committee on 11 September 2024.
What is the better way to answer an MW-style essay question?
A. List facts only and take no position
B. State your position first, then evidence with years and sources, address the counter-argument, and conclude
C. Recite whole passages from the course
D. Rest the argument on figures that sources disagree on
An essay needs a position, evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion; disputed figures should be flagged, not relied on.
